section_summary: This section covers Philippine views on Japan’s postwar position, followed by U.S. occupation reports on local government conferences in Kanagawa and Miyagi prefectures. Later documents address Japanese party politics, peace treaty debate, missionary work, and appeals to restore Ichiro Hatoyama to political life. The section ends with the opening of a despatch on the occupation’s economic and scientific work.

subfiles.title: Philippine foreign policy address, concluding pages
subfiles.about: The speaker sets out Philippine policy toward Japan and links economic development to international peace.
subfiles.summary: The Philippines supports Japanese self-sufficiency but opposes renewed dominance, presses reparations claims, and resists wider fishing rights and early international participation. The address calls for democratic safeguards before Japan’s admission to the community of nations and urges public support for Philippine foreign policy.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Kamakura civil affairs conference reports
subfiles.about: Transmits reports on a local autonomy conference at Kamakura.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a Yokohama cover letter and Richard Finn’s conference memorandum.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cover letter on the Kamakura conference
subfiles.about: Pilcher forwards Finn’s report and highlights local government problems.
subfiles.summary: Pilcher flags staffing, mayoral recalls, commissions, police secrecy, and reliance on Tokyo. He contrasts effective Kanagawa and Yokohama administration with alleged corruption and poor management in Kamakura.

subfiles.title: Civil Affairs Conference at Kamakura
subfiles.about: Finn reports on a November 9–10 conference about local autonomy.
subfiles.summary: Participants discussed municipal finance, education, policing, juvenile problems, and civic responsibility. Finn describes uneven administration in Kanagawa and concludes that local autonomy had made some progress but remained constrained by weak councils and dependence on Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Airgram on Democratic Party unification
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed unification of Japan’s Democratic factions and Yoshida’s response.
subfiles.summary: A Democratic Party figure called for party unity while rejecting merger with the Democratic Liberals; Prime Minister Yoshida reportedly said he would ignore the statement.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Shiogama civil affairs conference reports
subfiles.about: Transmits reports on the Shiogama local government conference.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Pilcher’s letter and Magistretti’s report on the Miyagi conference.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cover letter on the Shiogama conference
subfiles.about: Pilcher forwards Magistretti’s report on Miyagi.
subfiles.summary: Attributes difficulties with local autonomy in Miyagi to poverty and regional backwardness.

subfiles.title: Local Government Conference at Shiogama
subfiles.about: Magistretti examines local autonomy, civic participation, and economic conditions in Miyagi.
subfiles.summary: The report describes Shiogama’s port plans and conference discussions about mayoral recalls, policing, taxation, schools, and civic duties. It portrays Miyagi as poor and politically polarized, with conservative elites, disaffected younger residents, and women facing barriers to participation. Magistretti finds progress possible but expects a difficult struggle for local democracy.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cover letter on the Shiogama conference, duplicate
subfiles.about: Repeats Pilcher’s assessment of Magistretti’s Miyagi report.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the cover letter on page 13.

subfiles.title: Local Government Conference at Shiogama, duplicate excerpt
subfiles.about: Repeats the Shiogama report through its discussion of civic responsibility.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the report on pages 14–23, ending before its conclusions.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram, text illegible
subfiles.about: A filed airgram whose substantive text is not legible in the supplied OCR.
subfiles.summary: Only the airgram form and filing marks are discernible.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on peace treaty statements
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese discussions of peace treaty policy and Communist Party agitation.
subfiles.summary: A vice minister relayed concerns about Communist calls for an all-power peace treaty and troop withdrawal. The U.S. political adviser cautioned against public treaty discussion that could create misunderstandings abroad.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Marks a replacement record copy of Tokyo airgram A-351.
subfiles.summary: States that the action copy was not returned to central records.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on peace treaty statements, duplicate
subfiles.about: Repeats the report on Japanese peace treaty discussions.
subfiles.summary: Replacement copy of the airgram on pages 35–36, including the warning against extensive public treaty discussion.

subfiles.title: Incoming Tokyo airgram, largely illegible
subfiles.about: An incoming political airgram whose subject cannot be reliably recovered from the OCR.
subfiles.summary: The sender, date, and filing form remain partly legible; the message does not.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram on party politics, largely illegible
subfiles.about: A partly legible airgram concerning political party activity.
subfiles.summary: Scattered references to party and coalition politics survive.

subfiles.title: Airgram on a Japanese peace organisation
subfiles.about: Reports formation of a Japanese organisation advocating a peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Describes an inaugural meeting and plans to contact peace organisations abroad.

subfiles.title: Request for information on missionary work in Japan
subfiles.about: A Baptist convention asks about undertaking missionary work in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests information on conditions, possibilities, and requirements for a mission.

subfiles.title: Referral of missionary inquiry to the Army
subfiles.about: Asks the Army’s Reorientation Branch to answer the convention’s inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Carter’s request and asks Lynch’s office to supply the information.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of missionary inquiry
subfiles.about: Tells Carter that the Army has been asked to reply.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the December 20 letter and refers it to the Army.

subfiles.title: The Purge of Hatoyama Ichiro
subfiles.about: Forwards private appeals to lift Hatoyama’s purge and assesses their political context.
subfiles.summary: Alden describes Hatoyama’s estrangement from Yoshida, possible conservative realignment, and the obstacle posed by his direct SCAP purge. She passes on three letters without recommending intervention.

subfiles.title: Excerpt of letter from Kazuo Kojima
subfiles.about: Urges authorities to reconsider Hatoyama’s purge.
subfiles.summary: Kojima argues Japan needs Hatoyama’s political abilities and asks that his case reach American authorities.

subfiles.title: Excerpt of letter from Tsunego Baba
subfiles.about: Requests re-examination of Hatoyama’s purge.
subfiles.summary: Baba portrays Hatoyama as a liberal opponent of militarism and communism. He attributes the purge to misunderstanding and offers to testify for Hatoyama.

subfiles.title: Excerpt of letter from Gizo Tomabechi
subfiles.about: Advocates Hatoyama’s return to Japanese politics.
subfiles.summary: Tomabechi criticizes current parliamentary leadership and argues that Hatoyama could strengthen democratic opposition and counter Communist gains. He asks for SCAP review with State Department support.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Publication on Mission and Achievements of the Occupation in the Economic and Scientific Fields
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP study of occupation economic and scientific work.
subfiles.summary: The despatch highlights Japan’s trade gap, industrial production targets, fiscal reform, banking, foreign exchange controls, and subsidies. It quotes the study’s account of licensed foreign firms and the gradual transfer of exchange administration to Japanese authorities. The document continues beyond page 57.
